text:
maria: heads up — production inference pods in cluster-usa-east started seeing intermittent packet loss between nodes, looks like overlay (geneve) mostly between node-pool-gpu-1 and node-pool-gpu-2. 10-30% request failures for multi-gpu RPCs since ~08:05 UTC.
kevin: ack. any recent infra changes? mtu? kernel?
maria: no config rollouts. We did a small kernel patch on a few hosts yesterday (5.15 -> 5.15.106) but only on infra-utils nodes, not GPU nodes.
kevin: can you run a quick iperf3 and tcpdump from one of the affected pods -> other node host? also check host MTU and CNI tunnel MTU.
sam: running iperf3 now in UDP and TCP. TCP looks fine for short runs but UDP shows packet loss when above ~900Mbit.
sam: iperf3 -c 10.4.12.8 -u -b 1G -l 1400
sam: tcpdump on host showed a bunch of fragmented geneve packets and some NIC offload checksum mismatches:
```
12:23:11.456789 IP (tos 0x0, ttl 64, id 12345, offset 0, flags [DF]) 10.4.12.6 > 10.4.12.8: UDP, length 1600
12:23:11.456790  > geneve, proto 0x6558, vni 0x003456
12:23:11.456791 ... outer header size pushes it over 1500 and we see fragments at the host
```
maria: nodes show mtu 1500 on eth0, cilium tunnel mtu set to 1450. host NIC is Broadcom 57414.
kevin: Broadcoms have had issues with GSO/TSO and geneve before. can you collect `ethtool -k` and `dmesg | grep -i bnx2x` on the host? also `sysctl net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing`
sam: ethtool -k eth0 shows GSO: on, TSO: on, GRO: on. dmesg has a few `bnx2x` warnings about tx timeouts but nothing huge.
kevin: try disabling GSO/TCP segmentation offload temporarily on one host to reproduce: `ethtool -K eth0 gso off gro off tso off` and re-run iperf3.
maria: did that on node-12 (one side) and packet loss dropped to ~1-2% from ~18%. Looks promising.
ben: good find. we should decide whether to roll that cluster-wide or tune MTU. if GSO off fixes it maybe NIC driver bug with large geneve encapsulated packets.
nisha: we've seen similar in us-west2 last year — fixed by raising host MTU to 9000 and setting tunnel mtu accordingly. downside: not all tenants want jumbo frames, and cross-subnet paths can break.
irene: are we using RDMA or GPUDirect for inter-GPU comms? could RDMA/verbs be impacted by overlay?
maria: not RDMA. pods use gRPC over TCP for tensor sharding. so overlay fragmentation matters.
kevin: we need a short plan: 1) gather `ethtool -k`, `ip link show`, `ip -s link` from all affected hosts, 2) test GSO/TCO toggle impact across 3 nodes, 3) try MTU 9000 on a canary host (need TO network team), 4) consider switching cilium tunnel mode from geneve -> vxlan (compat check) or use direct routing if possible.
maria: starting collection now, attaching logs in case channel needs them. small note: pod-level pings show occasional 1-2ms spikes but loss correlates with large payloads.
kevin: also check conntrack and kube-proxy rules — but since it's payload-size related, offload/fragmentation is likelier. run `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` too. if PMTU discovery is disabled we'll see more fragmentation.
sam: `sysctl net.ipv4.ip_no_pmtu_disc` is 0 (enabled) on hosts.
maria: deploy-bot: canary rollout of 2 pods to fall back to single-GPU RPC (less fragmentation) — please monitor.
deploy-bot: canary rollout started for service/inference-canary (2 pods) at 08:28 UTC.
kevin: capture `tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/geneve-node12.pcap 'udp and port 6081'` (geneve default UDP port) and upload to the incident ticket.
sam: uploaded pcap (s3://redwood-debug/pcaps/1718654302-node12-geneve.pcap). shows large outer UDP length sometimes >1500 with DF off leading to fragmentation. also noticed NIC checksum offload flags set which make the kernel show bad checksums in tcpdump but packets still pass — tricky to interpret.
ben: summary so far: likely NIC driver + geneve encapsulation causing packetization issues (GSO/TSO interaction) leading to drops under high throughput. short-term: disable GSO/TCP offloading on GPU node-pool-hosts. medium-term: test MTU jumbo frames in staging and consult network team for host NIC firmware/drivers. long-term: consider moving latency-sensitive inter-pod traffic to hostNetwork or node-local direct routing (no overlay) for GPU pods.
maria: I'll prepare a runbook for the short-term patch (disable offloads + monitor) and open a P0 if loss >5% post-change.
nisha: also check firmware version on Broadcom NICs, vendor had a fix for geneve fragmentation last year.
irene: thanks all. please keep updates here. I'll add ops-oncall for monitor windows. :thumbsup:
maria: will post progress after the first cluster-wide offload disable (ETA 30m).
kevin: nice triage. remembered note: if we switch to vxlan we need to check kernel support and Cilium config; geneve supports more extensibility but we see this problem in both in past due to offload interaction.
maria: update (08:56 UTC) — disabled gso/gro/tso across 6 affected hosts; initial monitoring shows RPC failure rate down to baseline. still watching for side-effects on CPU.
kevin: good. open a ticket with network team for NIC fw update and test jumbo frames in staging. include pcap and iperf results.
maria: ticket created: NET-2145, attaching artifacts.
kevin: thanks — tagging this resolved for now until network team provides firmware/mtu plan.
maria: resolved for now, will keep channel posted if regressions appear. :white_check_mark:
